claims.claim: The chr_b singleton is *(0x0214BD80), a global pointer to a large 'battle resource manager' struct. Inside the arm9 battle-init loader (function 0x02075FBC, part of a ~1KB routine that sequentially loads koma.bin/komatxt.bin/kshape.bin/chr_b.bin/chr_s.bin/ability.bin/... into the SAME manager struct), the chr_b.bin file handle is opened (preceded by the filename load resolving to string 'bin/chr_b.bin' at 0x0209F5D4) and stored at manager+0xC (hit 0x020760F8), then handle->+4->vtable->[+0x2C] ('GetData') is virtual-called and its result -- the actual 60-byte-record array base -- is stored at manager+0x40 (hit 0x02076120). This is the ONE place in the ROM where chr_b's array pointer is established; every other confirmed chr_b consumer (13 more sites catalogued in this file) computes recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + index*0x3C from this cached pointer.

arm9 function 0x02077178 (hit 0x020771A0) reads chr_b record offsets +8(statA)/+0xA(statB)/+0xC(statC) as a 16-bit triple: recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + charIndex*0x3C, charIndex read from a character-context struct's own cached byte at +0x41. The triple is packed onto the stack and later compared (bare equality, not a threshold/tier check) against a per-technique data table entry -- this is a koma/technique stat-requirement eligibility matcher, not a movement/speed selector (matches the prior campaign's movement.round1 finding). This getter is called from ov5 (menu, 0x0215A31C) and from arm9 0x020772E4 (see next claim), i.e. it is core simulation code, not ov5-exclusive.

arm9 function 0x020772E4 (hit 0x02077310) walks a per-character 'active technique/hitbox' linked list at charStruct+0x558 and, for each node, reads chr_b record offset 0x10+4*idx (CombatStat(idx+1)Value, LOW byte; recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + PassiveIndex*0x3C) and folds it (with a clamp against 0x4000) into an 'attack property' value CACHED into the active-move/technique struct's own +0x16 field (duplicated to +0x18). Separately, arm9 0x020784E4 (a tiny leaf, called from ov6's hit-resolution function 0x02158B20 at call site 0x02158D8C) reads that SAME move-struct's +0x16 and +0x18 fields and compares them -- i.e. the chr_b-derived CombatStat value that reaches ov6's hit-resolution path is a value CACHED at technique-setup time, not read live from chr_b during the hit check itself. This directly supports the prompt's cache-at-load/cache-at-setup hypothesis, generalized from 'weight/knockback' to 'attack-property' scaling.
open_questions: Confirm at runtime that the move-struct written by 0x020772E4 (charStruct+0x558 list node) is the SAME object later read via charStruct+0x56C in 0x020784E4 -- the two offsets (+0x558 list vs +0x56C pointer) are close but not proven identical here; if they differ, the cache-to-hitcheck link is only structurally suggestive, not proven.

claims.claim: arm9 function 0x02077768 (hit 0x020777A8) loops over chr_b record offsets +3..+7 (CharId, then all 4 bytes of the 'Flags' u32) ONE BYTE AT A TIME (recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + PassiveIndex*0x3C), using each byte's raw VALUE as an index into the manager+0x50 ability/passive-effect lookup table to select a per-byte dispatch (no-op / direct call to 0x2077a74 / jump-table call through a second table). No instruction anywhere in the 97 xref hits to 0x0214BD80 reads offset +4 as a single 32-bit load -- Flags is consumed exclusively as up to 5 independent byte-sized ability/effect IDs (bytes 3,4,5,6,7), not a single bitmask. This is a MISMATCH worth flagging against jus_files/exported_combat/chr_b.json's schema, which models offset+4 as one 'flags' integer field.
claims.gdb_check: break 0x020777CC (the ldrb that fetches each of the 5 bytes) during a match with several different characters/techniques active, and dump the fetched byte plus the resulting manager+0x50 table lookup to confirm these bytes really do select distinct ability/passive effects rather than being read as a combined bitmask elsewhere at runtime.

claims.claim: arm9 function 0x02077C0C (hit 0x02077C10) is a 'cache chr_b fields into the live move/technique struct' routine, called at technique-setup time (0 direct bl callers found in the whole ROM -- reached only via a per-move-type function-pointer/jump-table dispatch, i.e. core simulation code, not ov5- or ov6-exclusive). recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + PassiveIndex*0x3C (PassiveIndex from charStruct+0x41); techIdx = (a per-technique index read from charStruct+0x34's own +8 field) - 3. It copies: FormType(+0)->moveStruct+0x13, Tier(+1)->+0x11, KomaSize(+2)->+0x10, CombatStat(techIdx+1)Value low/high byte (+0x10+4*techIdx / +0x11+4*techIdx)->+0x16(<<6, duplicated to +0x18)/+0x49(with a 'default to 4 if zero' fallback), CombatStat(techIdx+1)Mod low/high byte (+0x12+4*techIdx / +0x13+4*techIdx)->+0x14/+0x15, TextIds[0] (+0x30, fixed)->+0x2E, and TextIds[1+techIdx] (+0x32+2*techIdx)->+0x30. The TextIds[0]-vs-TextIds[1..5] split strongly implies textIds[0]=character-name text id and textIds[1..5]=per-technique(move) name text ids (5 techniques matches the 5-iteration eligibility loop bound seen in claim covering 0x02077178/0x020772E4).
open_questions: Confirm the exact triggering event for 0x02077C0C (which per-move-type jump table slot points here) via GDB watchpoint on the write to move-struct+0x16, to establish whether this runs at technique SELECTION time (menu-adjacent) or technique EXECUTION time (pure battle).

claims.claim: Two small leaf getters sit back-to-back in arm9 ROM, both reading chr_b's BattleParams region (record offset 0x24-0x2F, 12 bytes, C# field BattleCharacterEntry.BattleParams): (1) address 0x02078514 (hit) computes recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + PassiveIndex*0x3C and reads offset 0x24+2*idx as a ushort (treating all 12 BattleParams bytes as ushort[6]); (2) address 0x0207853C (hit) uses the identical recordBase/stride setup but reads offset 0x2C+idx as a raw byte (treating BattleParams' last 4 bytes as byte[]). The SAME 12-byte blob is thus read with two DIFFERENT element sizes by two different getters -- consistent with the C# converter's own uncertainty comment that BattleParams' true structure/meaning is unclear.

ANSWERS Q3 (positive half). The two chr_b BattleParams getters (0x02078514, 0x0207853C -- see prior claim) have exactly ONE caller each in the entire ROM (confirmed via `xrefs-to 0x02078514` / `xrefs-to 0x0207853C`, each returning a single branch reference), and both callers are inside the SAME ov11 function 0x02174330, which `query.py strings ov11` identifies as part of the Battle-AI subsystem (debug strings 'BattleAI_Create', 'BattleAIObj_CreateBranchNode', 'BattleAI_JobAtkBrh.cpp' etc. found in ov11, no menu/UI strings). At 0x021746E0, ov11 calls 0x02078514 (chr_b BattleParams as ushort[6]) and loops 14 times building a per-technique 'availability' bitmask; at 0x02174724 it calls 0x0207853C (BattleParams tail as byte[]) and stores the result into a per-slot AI range/facing table used by later range-threshold comparisons (0x50/0xA0) in the same function. This is a genuine BATTLE-TIME (CPU decision-tree) chr_b consumer -- distinct from, and additional to, ov5's menu-side FormType selectors and the arm9 core-simulation cache-copy functions.

A family of near-identical ov5 (menu) 'special form' dispatch getters reads chr_b record offset +0 (FormType) whenever a selector struct's byte+0xB high nibble == 3: 0x0214D944 (hit 0x0214D95C, inside a koma-hand render/sort-key builder that ALSO reads chr_s at manager+0x48 for other nibble values), 0x0214DC18 (hit 0x0214DC28, sibling render/sort-key builder used for a returned selection count), and 0x0214E480 (hits 0x0214E4A0/0x0214E4D0, the KNOWN ground-truth 'special form' selector, called twice due to the compiler re-loading the same pool constant). All four compute recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + koma-byte-derived-index*0x3C and read a bare byte at offset 0 (FormType). This corroborates FormType=offset 0 (matches chr_b.json 'formType') via 3 independent call sites beyond the one already known.

Two more ov5 getters (0x0214E238 hit 0x0214E258, and 0x0214E284 hit 0x0214E2A8) appear to belong to the SAME 'special form nibble==3 -> chr_b FormType' family as claim C7a: both cleanly establish recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + koma-byte*0x3C via a mov #0x3c + smulbb sequence identical to 0x0214E480's. However, in the pre-built disasm database, the bytes immediately after each smulbb (where the final 'ldrb r?,[r?,r0]' offset-0 read would be) decode as short Thumb-looking instructions/branches rather than the expected ARM tail -- almost certainly a shared-tail-veneer artifact in the listing rather than genuine Thumb code (ov5 is otherwise pure ARM). Because the query.py `disasm` output for those exact addresses does not show a clean 'ldrb' instruction, record offset 0 is PLAUSIBLE for these two sites by strong structural analogy, not CONFIRMED_STATIC by direct quote.
claims.gdb_check: break 0x0214E268 and 0x0214E2B8 (the mla/smulbb instructions) during a menu session that hits a 'special form' character (selector+0xB high nibble==3), single-step 2-3 instructions past the breakpoint, and confirm the CPU actually executes an ldrb-with-register-offset (reading chr_b record+0) rather than diverging into some other path -- this would resolve whether the Thumb-looking bytes are a disasm-listing artifact or a genuine (surprising) mode switch.
open_questions: Is the apparent Thumb-mode decode at 0x0214E26C/0x0214E2BC a pre-built listing/database defect, or does the ROM genuinely BX into Thumb code here? Neither this campaign nor the prior one has GDB-verified it.

claims.claim: ANSWERS Q3 (negative half, direct hits). The ONLY literal_load reference to 0x0214BD80 inside ov6 in the entire ROM is 0x0215FAEC, inside a per-frame entity/listener dispatch function (0x0215FAC4). It reads manager+0x50 (the SAME ability/passive-effect lookup table consumed by arm9 0x020775BC/0x020777A8/0x0207783C/0x02078040/0x020781BC) to select a per-entity handler via an ov6-local jump table (pool constant 0x02172210) -- it does NOT dereference manager+0x40 (chr_b's own array). claims.claim: ov6's hit-resolution function 0x02158B20 (876 bytes) calls arm9 0x020784E4 directly at call site 0x02158D8C ('bl #0x20784e4'). 0x020784E4 reads the active-move/technique struct's +0x16 and +0x18 fields (via charStruct+0x56C) and returns a clamp/threshold comparison result -- the SAME +0x16/+0x18 fields that arm9 0x020772E4 (see earlier claim) writes from chr_b's CombatStatNValue field at technique-setup time. This is the concrete ov6-side half of the cache-at-setup chain: ov6's actual battle hit-resolution code consumes a chr_b-derived value, but only via this pre-computed cache, never via a fresh literal_load of 0x0214BD80 inside ov6 itself.

The one literal_load hit to 0x0214BD80 that appears directly inside ov11 (0x021752B8, inside AI branch/command-node function 0x021751CC) reads chr_s (manager+0x48, stride 0x14=20 bytes, indexed by PassiveIndex from *(sl)->+0x41) for a range/facing evaluation -- NOT chr_b's own +0x40 array. chr_b IS consumed elsewhere in ov11 (see claim about 0x021746E0/0x02174724 in function 0x02174330), but that consumption is via `bl` into arm9 helper getters, not a direct literal_load of the manager singleton inside ov11.

COMPLETENESS: the remaining 43 arm9 literal_load hits to 0x0214BD80 (out of 51 total arm9 hits; 8 are chr_b-touching, covered by earlier claims) all resolve to OTHER fields of the SAME 'battle resource manager' singleton, never to chr_b's own +0x40 array. Grouped by function: 0x02075FBC (the loader, 25 remaining hits) touches the manager's own allocation/mode-object slot (+0), the koma sub-object and its handle (+0x30/+4/+0x34), kshape's handle+data (+8/+0x38), chr_s's handle (+0x10, data covered elsewhere), the next resource's handle+data (+0x18/+0x50, an ability/passive-effect lookup table reused battle-wide), several more resource handles/data slots (+0x1C/+0x20/+0x24/+0x2C/+0x44[212B table]/+0x4C[36B table]/+0x54[12B table]/+0x60), two allocated koma-filter-list buffers (+0x58/+0x5C), and a large +0x64.. sub-object zero-init region plus the +0x18E4/+0x1911/+0x1912 'match config' sub-struct fields also touched by 0x02076510 (combo/chain-limit thresholds, 4 hits), 0x02078038/0x020790F0(x3)/0x02078CD4 (mode-config gates), and 0x020781BC (a standalone flag getter). 0x0207698C, 0x02076C98, 0x02076D00, 0x02077584, 0x02077768's second hit, 0x02077CB8, and 0x02078110 touch koma(+0x34)/kshape(+0x38)/koma(+0x30)/ability-table(+0x50 x2)/chr_s(+0x48 x2) respectively. claims.claim: ANSWERS Q3 (synthesis). Is any chr_b getter reachable from ov6 battle code (e.g. 0x02158B20)? NUANCED YES, via two distinct mechanisms, plus one clear negative: (1) NEGATIVE for direct access: the sole ov6 literal_load hit to 0x0214BD80 (0x0215FAEC) never touches chr_b's own +0x40 array (it reads a sibling ability-table slot, manager+0x50); no ov6 code anywhere loads the chr_b array pointer itself. (2) POSITIVE via caching: ov6's actual hit-resolution function 0x02158B20 calls arm9 0x020784E4 (call site 0x02158D8C), which reads an attack-property value that arm9 0x020772E4/0x02077C0C previously CACHED from chr_b's CombatStatNValue field (+0x10+4*i) into a move/technique struct at technique-setup time -- i.e. the value ov6 consumes during hit resolution is pre-computed from chr_b, not read live from it, exactly matching the prompt's cache-at-load hypothesis (generalized from weight/knockback to attack-property scaling). (3) POSITIVE via live battle-time read (a DIFFERENT overlay than ov6): chr_b's BattleParams field (+0x24, +0x2C) IS read LIVE, every time it's needed, by the Battle-AI overlay ov11 (function 0x02174330, calling arm9 getters 0x02078514/0x0207853C) to build technique-availability/range data for CPU opponent decision-making -- this runs during actual battles (it is not menu code; ov11's only strings are Battle-AI debug labels) even though it is architecturally a separate overlay from ov6's hit-resolution code. Overall: chr_b's per-frame/per-hit-critical fields (CombatStatNValue) are cached rather than live-read by the time ov6 needs them, but chr_b is NOT universally cache-only -- the AI subsystem reads it live. If the question is narrowed to 'only ov5 vs ov6', the answer is that every OTHER confirmed chr_b consumer besides the AI (statA/B/C eligibility matcher, FormType selectors, record-cache function, flags-as-ability dispatcher) is core arm9 simulation code or ov5 menu code, never ov6 directly.
open_questions: Whether the move/technique struct written by 0x02077C0C/0x020772E4 (via charStruct+0x558 list nodes) and read by 0x020784E4 (via charStruct+0x56C) are proven the same object at runtime is the one remaining structural gap in the ov6 cache-chain argument (see the open_questions on the 0x020772E4 claim).

suggested_next_angles: ClassId (+0xE) has zero observed direct consumers among the 97 xref hits to 0x0214BD80 -- either trace it via a different access mechanism (e.g. a value cached at parse time into a separate table never touching the raw literal), or confirm via GDB that it is genuinely dead data in this ROM build.

The CharId(+3)/Flags(+4-7)-as-ability-index reinterpretation (claim on 0x02077768) should be GDB-verified against known character/technique combinations to turn 'MISMATCH (candidate)'/'MISMATCH (confirmed)' into a concrete field-rename recommendation for jus_files/exported_combat/chr_b.json and src/JUS.Tool/Combat/Formats/BattleCharacterEntry.cs.

The apparent Thumb-mode decode artifact immediately after the smulbb/mla record-index computation in ov5 functions 0x0214E238 and 0x0214E284 (and briefly in 0x0214DEE4/0x0214E1E0) recurred across at least 4 independent functions -- worth a targeted look at the disasm database build (disasm_db.py) for a systematic shared-tail-veneer misalignment bug in this address range, rather than treating each occurrence as an isolated anomaly.

The open structural gap in the Q3 cache-chain argument (does charStruct+0x558's list-node object equal the charStruct+0x56C pointer target?) is answerable with a single GDB session: break on the write side (0x02077368/0x02077C9C region) and the read side (0x020784E8) during one attack and compare pointers.

ov11's Battle-AI subsystem (function 0x02174330 and its 19 callees) is a promising, previously-uncatalogued reachability path into chr_b for a future tracer unit -- this campaign only followed the two BattleParams getters found via caller-tracing; a dedicated pass over 0x02174330's other callees might find additional live chr_b reads (e.g. of statA/B/C or CombatStatN) that were missed because they don't literal_load 0x0214BD80 directly inside ov11.
